questions.stem: Export of ions from nucleus to extracellular matrix involve all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Rat proteins

The export of ions from the nucleus to the extracellular matrix involves processes like the activity of exportins, local signals, and potentially other cellular components, but it does not involve rat proteins.

questions.stem: Stimulus for secretion of Mullerian inhibiting substance is present on which chromosome:

The stimulus for secretion of Mullerian inhibiting substance (MIS), also known as Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), is present on the B. Y chromosome.

questions.stem: In hypovolemic shock what occurs in kidney:
questions.solutionHtml:
Afferent arteriolar resistance increased
  • Kidney responds to shock by increasing afferent arteriolar resistance.
  • In fact both afferent and efferent arterioles are constricted, but the efferent vessels are constricted to a greater degree.
  • The glomerular filtration rate is depressed, but renal plasma flow is decreased to a greater extent, so that the filtration fraction increases.


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no 537.

questions.solutionHtml:
PGE2

Among the given options, PGE2 (Prostaglandin E2) is an endogenous pyrogen. Endogenous pyrogens are substances produced by the body that can cause fever.

questions.answerText: Tricuspid valve bulging into right atrium during right ventricular isovolumetric contraction
questions.solutionHtml:
Tricuspid valve bulging into right atrium during right ventricular isovolumetric contraction

During the isovolumetric contraction phase, the ventricles are contracting, but the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonic valves) are still closed. As the ventricles contract, the pressure within the ventricles increases.

This increased pressure causes the tricuspid valve, which lies between the right atrium and right ventricle, to bulge backward into the right atrium. This bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium creates a temporary increase in jugular venous pressure, leading to the C wave in the JVP waveform.

questions.stem: Body fat cannot be measured by?
questions.solutionHtml:
Body density
  • Body fat can be measured using various methods, including body density (B), total body calcium (C), and waist-hip ratio (D).
  • However, measuring total body water (A) is not a direct method of assessing body fat. Instead, it is a measurement used to estimate fat-free mass or lean body mass.

questions.stem: Components responsible for countercurrent mechanism in kidney are all except:

options.label: B
options.text: Water outflow in thin descending limb

options.label: C

questions.answerText: Sodium outflow in thin ascending limb
questions.solutionHtml:
Sodium outflow in thin ascending limb
  • Thin ascending limb is not a component of the countercurrent mechanism.
  • The loop of Henle functions as countercurrent multipliers and vasa recta as countercurrent exchangers.

questions.stem: Glucose is absorbed in the intestine by?
questions.solutionHtml:
Secondary active transport

Glucose is absorbed in the intestine by secondary active transport (sodium co-transport).

DMT1

Transport of Fe2+ into the enterocytes occurs via divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1), through an active transport process.

questions.stem: Aldosterone synthesis is stimulated by which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hyperkalemia

Hyperkalemia and activation of the renin-angiotensin system are the most potent stimulators of aldosterone secretion.

questions.stem: ACTH secretion is increased by all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Aldosterone

The only option that does not increase ACTH secretion is C. Aldosterone. Aldosterone is primarily involved in sodium and water retention and does not directly affect ACTH levels.
